purpose: Independently articulated cart, canvas cover, wheel, dock and supply hatch.
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production sprite-parts atlas for a painterly side-scrolling survival game. Reference image is STYLE ONLY: match especially its small worn canvas tent, the subtle warm canvas folds, weathered timber, hand-painted iron and clearly readable midtones. New image with genuine transparent background, 1536x1536 or larger square. Six fully separate isolated parts in a spacious 2-column by 3-row layout, with very wide transparent gutters; no touching, labels, ground shadows, characters or backdrop. Strict orthographic side elevation, no perspective. Top left: small wooden handcart chassis, weathered plank box with iron fittings and a leftward pushing handle, NO wheels and NO canopy, width to height about 84:55. Top right: long low olive-brown canvas windscreen/canopy stretched on a light wooden frame, the shelter extends BACKWARDS to the LEFT from its rightmost upright, wide enough to shelter two crouched children behind the cart, width to height 190:92; rich stitched seams and broad readable folds, dark underneath but not black. Middle left: a single complete circular wood-spoked wheel with iron rim, exactly round and side-on, isolated for rotation. Middle right: a dock ratchet mechanism and wooden bump stop, width to height58:70, hand-crank and obvious toothed iron pawl. Bottom left: low small worn wooden supply cabinet body with rusty corner brackets and warm visible empty interior, NO lid, width to height72:52. Bottom right: the cabinet's separate long horizontal plank lid with metal hinges, width to height72:10. Render all parts generously large within their cells with crisp silhouette edges, real transparent space, opaque material interiors. Museum-quality painterly oil/gouache craft, fine but restrained surface marks, warm top-left light and soft cool reflected light. No harsh glossy CGI, no black crushed detail, no extra loose parts. This is a usable mechanical cutout atlas; each separate component must remain complete and unobstructed.
integration: Original generated RGBA retained without raster modifications; runtime atlas regions and deforming meshes use these pixels; mipmaps enabled.
